answer: Retrospective Behavioral Clustering. Agents are grouped by similarity of action timing, tool-call sequences, and payload fingerprints; a violet flag marks clusters whose members act in lockstep. Enforcement: treat the whole cluster as one identity for reward and rate limits. To evade, an attacker must diversify each puppet's behavior continuously, raising per-identity operational cost by roughly the price of a pearl—constant retraining and timing jitter per account—while a canyon of distinct behavior histories makes coordination unprofitable.
